evidence: src/domain/DomainError.ts: `class DomainError extends Error` is the single error type, used by Project, User and Task constructors and by Task.markDone
src/domain/TaskStatus.ts: `type TaskStatus = "todo" | "in progress" | "done"` and `isTaskStatus` keep the status vocabulary in one file
src/domain/Task.ts: `markDone()` alone enforces the rule that a task already done cannot be marked done again; it stores `taskStatus` as the `TaskStatus` type
src/domain/Repositories.ts: `UserRepository`, `ProjectRepository` and `TaskRepository` are ports typed against the domain entities; `findByProject` reuses `TaskStatus`
src/domain/Project.ts and src/domain/User.ts: each constructor checks only its own entity's invariant (id and non-blank name)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the task-management domain model. It holds the entities (Project, User, Task), a value type (TaskStatus), the repository ports (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository) and a shared error type (DomainError). Every entity reports invariant violations through DomainError, so the error abstraction is used consistently. Each invariant lives in one place. Task owns its own creation checks and the markDone transition. TaskStatus owns the set of allowed status values and its type guard. Repositories.ts uses the domain types (Task, TaskStatus, Project, User) and does not redefine them. Project and User run similar id/name checks, but they are separate invariants for separate entities, so this is not a single rule copied in two places. TaskStatus.ts repeats the literals in both the type and the isTaskStatus guard, but both sit in the same file, so the rule stays in one place. No file goes around the module's own abstractions.
